channels.name: soc2-audit
channels.topic: Evidence, findings and the audit window

documents.content:
# Lumen Labs renewal

Usage is up 61% year on year. Two compliance workspaces added in March.

## Reliability

Lease heartbeat lands in 3.2 and holds at 268,000 rows on our fixture. Callan reruns their own largest export on Thursday; use their number, not ours.

## Open and unfixed

Issue 903: a cancelled run can leave a partial object in the destination bucket. Say this out loud on the call. Do not let it be a surprise later.

## Billing

August invoice is above true usage because of the metering fault. Credit note is coming. Rowan has already told Priya.
documents.name: Lumen renewal brief.md

documents.content:
# Release 3.2 gate

Go requires BOTH:

1. Issue 902, lease heartbeat, merged and verified above 250k rows.
2. Issue 903, cancellation cleanup, merged with the defer ordering fixed.

The release note stays conditional until both are true. We have written “fixed” once before for 902 when only the timeout had moved; that is how a year passed with the bug still open.
documents.name: Release 3.2 gate.md

documents.content:
# 12 August — exports queued for 41 minutes

## What happened

A burst of scheduled exports arrived faster than the autoscaler added workers. Queue depth peaked at 4,100.

## Impact

No data lost. No export failed. Every export in the window was late. Brightwell, Orchard and Halcyon were affected.

## The one action

A pre-warmed floor of workers during known peak hours. Issue 911.

## What we are not doing

Adding an alert on queue depth alone. We already had one; it fired and told us something we could not act on quickly enough.
documents.name: Postmortem 12 August.md

documents.content:
# Metering overcount

Exports that resume emit a second metering record for rows before the resume point. Issue 905.

## Sequence

1. Billing run on hold. Nobody is re-billed before reconciliation.
2. Reconciliation script reviewed by an engineer before it touches production metering.
3. Every affected account is told by us before they notice.
4. Credit notes.

Step 3 is not optional and does not wait for step 4.
documents.name: Metering overcount — handling note.md

documents.content:
# Engineer onboarding

Day one: accounts, laptop, buddy.

Day two: staging access. This is the slowest step and has taken up to nine days. Priyanka now owns it.

Week one: ship one small change to production.

Week two: one on-call shadow shift.
documents.name: Engineer onboarding.md

documents.content:
# 2028 pricing

A usage-based tier for large exporters.

## Rule

No customer moves to a worse price without a conversation first. This is not negotiable and is not a marketing decision.

## Sequence

Per-account comparison, then conversations, then announcement. Not the other way round.
documents.name: 2028 pricing — working note.md

documents.content:
# Open audit items

- 906: destination changes are not audited. Scoped narrowly on purpose so it lands in three weeks.
- 920: webhook signing key rotation, with a dual-key window.
- 913: closed and verified 4 August.

Widen auditing to every privileged action after the November window, not before it.
documents.name: SOC 2 open items.md

documents.content:
# Stuck export lease

On-call has resolved this from memory three times. Writing it down.

1. Confirm the worker is gone, not slow.
2. Release the lease.
3. Check the destination for a partial object BEFORE restarting the export. Issue 903 means the partial object survives.
4. Restart.

Step 3 is the one people forget.
documents.name: Runbook: stuck export lease.md

mail.body_text:
Maya,

Before Tuesday I need two things in writing. First, whether scheduled exports at our volume are reliable in 3.2. Second, what happens to a partially written file if we cancel a run.

I am not asking for perfection. I am asking for the real answer so I can plan around it.

Priya
mail.snippet: Before Tuesday I need two things in writing. First, whether scheduled exports at our volume are reliable in 3.
mail.subject: Renewal and export reliability

mail.body_text:
Priya,

You will get both in writing before the call.

On the first: with the lease heartbeat in 3.2 we have three clean runs at 268,000 rows on our fixture. Callan has offered to run your largest saved export against a flag account this week, which gives you your number rather than ours.

On the second: today a cancelled run can leave a partial object in your bucket. That is issue 903 and it is not closed. Until it is, treat a cancelled run as needing a manual check of the destination.

Maya
mail.snippet: You will get both in writing before the call.
mail.subject: Re: Renewal and export reliability

mail.body_text:
That is the answer I wanted. Callan will run ours on Thursday.

The partial-object behaviour is workable if it is documented. It is not workable as a surprise.

Priya
mail.snippet: The partial-object behaviour is workable if it is documented. It is not workable as a surprise.
mail.subject: Re: Renewal and export reliability

mail.body_text:
Priya,

We found a metering fault before you did, and I would rather tell you now than have you find it on the invoice.

Exports that resume were counted twice for the rows before the resume point. Your August invoice is above your true usage. We have put the billing run on hold, we are reconciling, and a credit note will follow.

I do not have a date for the credit note yet. You will have one this week.

Rowan
mail.snippet: We found a metering fault before you did, and I would rather tell you now than have you find it on the invoice
mail.subject: Invoice amount is above your actual usage

mail.body_text:
Thank you for saying so first. Send the corrected usage when you have it; we will hold payment until then.

Priya
mail.snippet: Priya
mail.subject: Re: Invoice amount is above your actual usage

mail.body_text:
We renamed a column in the source system on 6 August. The Northstar sync kept running and simply stopped carrying that column. No error, no warning.

This is clinical data. I need to know which runs were affected before I need the fix.

Nadia
mail.snippet: This is clinical data. I need to know which runs were affected before I need the fix.
mail.subject: Renamed column dropped from your clinical sync

mail.body_text:
Understood, and you are right about the order.

We are producing the list of affected runs first. The behaviour change -- failing the sync instead of dropping the column -- is issue 909 and is a smaller job than the report.

I will send the affected-run list before the fix date.

Kwame
mail.snippet: We are producing the list of affected runs first. The behaviour change -- failing the sync instead of dropping
mail.subject: Re: Renamed column dropped from your clinical sync

mail.body_text:
Our compliance sign-off is held. We see duplicate rows whenever a chunk is retried.

Our date is the end of September. Can you tell me whether that is realistic?

Anders
mail.snippet: Our date is the end of September. Can you tell me whether that is realistic?
mail.subject: Duplicate rows after retried chunks

mail.body_text:
It is realistic. The cause is known: the chunk writer records progress after the write instead of before, so a retry replays the last chunk. That is issue 904.

The fix is small and the testing is not, because we want a test that kills a worker mid-chunk before it merges. I will give you a date once that test exists.

Samira
mail.snippet: The fix is small and the testing is not, because we want a test that kills a worker mid-chunk before it merges
mail.subject: Re: Duplicate rows after retried chunks

mail.body_text:
The export history page has stopped loading for us. Our regulatory reporting window opens on 4 September and this page is part of the evidence we produce.

Cormac
mail.snippet: Cormac
mail.subject: Export history page and the reporting window

mail.body_text:
It is the run count -- 61,300 historical runs, and the page computes its summary from all of them. Issue 907.

The fix is a summary table plus a backfill. We are treating 4 September as the date, not as a target.

Keiko
mail.snippet: The fix is a summary table plus a backfill. We are treating 4 September as the date, not as a target.
mail.subject: Re: Export history page and the reporting window

mail.body_text:
Interim report attached in the shared folder. Two items remain open on your side: destination changes are not written to the audit log, and the webhook signing key is past its rotation date.

Both are closable before the November window if they are started now.

Lena
mail.snippet: Both are closable before the November window if they are started now.
mail.subject: Interim audit findings

mail.body_text:
Both are open issues on our board, 906 and 920. Destination auditing is scoped narrowly on purpose so it lands in three weeks rather than three months; we will widen it after the window.

Zara
mail.snippet: Zara
mail.subject: Re: Interim audit findings

mail.body_text:
Postmortem is in relay-runbooks.

Summary: a burst of scheduled exports arrived faster than the autoscaler added workers. Queue depth peaked at 4,100. No data was lost and no export failed; every one was late.

The single action that would have prevented it is a pre-warmed floor of workers during known peak hours. That is issue 911.

Ingrid
mail.snippet: Summary: a burst of scheduled exports arrived faster than the autoscaler added workers. Queue depth peaked at
mail.subject: Postmortem: exports queued for 41 minutes on 12 August

mail.body_text:
Clear and useful. Make 911 a real task with an owner and a date, not a backlog item.

Jon
mail.snippet: Jon
mail.subject: Re: Postmortem: exports queued for 41 minutes on 12 August

mail.body_text:
Where are we with a Snowflake destination? Our warehouse team keeps asking and I keep saying soon.

Jana
mail.snippet: Jana
mail.subject: Snowflake destination

mail.body_text:
Design is agreed and the work is scheduled behind one dependency: the connector uses the same chunk writer as issue 904, which currently replays its last chunk on retry. Building on that first would build the bug into a new connector.

I would rather give you a real date after 904 closes than a hopeful one now.

Ben
mail.snippet: I would rather give you a real date after 904 closes than a hopeful one now.
mail.subject: Re: Snowflake destination

mail.body_text:

Nina

mail.subject: Trial usage counted against the paid limit

mail.body_text:
That is our fault -- trial usage is being metered against the paid limit. Issue 917.

I have lifted your limit manually so you are unblocked today, and the metering fix is with the billing team.

Nathan

mail.subject: Re: Trial usage counted against the paid limit

issues.body: Harbor Mobility sees duplicate rows after a retried chunk. The chunk writer records progress after the write instead of before, so a retry replays the last chunk.
